cases.prompt: The Supervisor just confirmed an orchestrator spawn for project acme-portal — record the Run row in ralph_runs.
cases.expected_behavior: Govern an FR-009 spawn INSERT: require project_slug, seed_path, spawned_at, orchestrator_pid; status born 'running'; metadata carries the process-start-time disambiguator; via the registry.py record_run mechanism.
cases.rationale: FR-009 spawn-row-at-spawn is the first of the two write points; required-field coverage is the core positive case.

cases.prompt: The orchestrator for acme-portal exited with INITIATIVE_COMPLETE — reconcile its ralph_runs row to terminal.
cases.expected_behavior: Govern an FR-011 terminal reconciliation UPDATE: set status='complete', terminated_at, and summed exact-decimal terminal_cost_usd; target only the currently-running row; via registry.py update_run_status.
cases.rationale: FR-011 terminal reconciliation is the second write point; the clean-completion acceptance criterion.

cases.prompt: An orchestrator hit its budget ceiling and exited on the budget-exhausted code. What status does its ralph_runs row get?
cases.expected_behavior: Map the exit code to status='budget_exhausted' (FR-012), explicitly distinct from 'failed'; never collapse the two.
cases.rationale: FR-012 exit-code mapping with budget_exhausted kept distinct from failed — the spec's named acceptance criterion.

cases.prompt: Should ralph_runs.project_slug have a hard foreign key to projects so the DB enforces the owning-project link?
cases.expected_behavior: No — FR-010 is a deliberate soft reference resolving to exactly one projects.project_id with NO hard FK; proposing a hard FK is a design change requiring re-gate (HALT).
cases.rationale: FR-010 soft-reference discipline; guards against drifting to a hard FK (OL-3 open modelling stance).

cases.prompt: The Supervisor restarted and found a ralph_runs row still marked running. How do we re-attach to that orchestrator?
cases.expected_behavior: Re-attach by recorded orchestrator_pid PLUS the metadata process-start-time disambiguator (FR-013); if both do not confirm the live process, reconcile the Run as 'failed'. Pid alone is insufficient (process-reuse hazard).
cases.rationale: FR-013 re-attach by recorded identity disambiguated against pid reuse.

cases.prompt: Can we just store the summed run cost as a Python float in terminal_cost_usd to keep it simple?
cases.expected_behavior: HALT/refuse — FR-014/NFR-007 require exact NUMERIC preserving cent precision; a float is a defect, not a rounding choice. Anti-guess: never store an approximated value.
cases.rationale: FR-014/NFR-007 exact-decimal anti-guess case; a float store is rejected, never silently accepted.

cases.prompt: Let's add a last_iteration_at heartbeat column to ralph_runs and update it every orchestrator iteration so we can see liveness.
cases.expected_behavior: HALT — §5.6 forbids a per-iteration liveness column on ralph_runs; status moves only at spawn and terminal reconciliation. Freshness is the event stream's last phase_complete (Event-Log §15), not a ralph_runs column.
cases.rationale: §5.6 no-liveness-column boundary; guards against introducing a third write point / freshness store.

cases.prompt: Can the running orchestrator itself write its own ralph_runs status row as it goes?
cases.expected_behavior: No — NFR-006 sole-writer: only the conforming Supervisor mechanism (registry.py) writes ralph_runs; no orchestrator Run, role skill, or Executor session writes a row directly. HALT the direct write.
cases.rationale: NFR-006 sole-writer discipline, mirroring cf-followup-tracker's exclusivity for followups.

cases.prompt: I'm editing Ralph_Loop_Outer_Loop_Spec section 5.4 to reword the FR-011 acceptance criterion.
cases.expected_behavior: Does NOT trigger — editing the governing spec is cf-spec-writer's job. This skill enforces the spec's ralph_runs contract; it does not author the spec (spec-enforcer anti-trigger).
cases.rationale: Spec-enforcer anti-trigger: must not fire on edits to its own governing document, only on ralph_runs writes.

cases.prompt: Ingest this Issues report and insert the new follow-up rows into the tracker.
cases.expected_behavior: Does NOT trigger — followups rows are cf-followup-tracker's domain. This skill is the sole writer for ralph_runs only, not followups.
cases.rationale: Negative/neighbour-skill case: the precedent skill cf-followup-tracker owns followups; this skill must not over-trigger onto a different table.

cases.prompt: Record a spawn Run row, but the project_slug 'acme' matches two rows in projects.
cases.expected_behavior: HALT — FR-010 requires project_slug to resolve to exactly one projects.project_id; zero or many is an unresolved reference. Surface the ambiguity; never guess a Project. Bad-source precondition.
cases.rationale: Bad-source / input-precondition case: an unresolvable soft reference halts rather than writing on a guessed Project.

cases.expected_behavior: HALT — 'timed_out' is outside the ralph_runs_status_check set (running | complete | budget_exhausted | failed | halted); the write is rejected before it reaches the DB. Never coerce to a near-value. A wedged-but-alive Run maps to 'halted'; a gone process maps to 'failed'.
cases.rationale: Anti-guess case: an out-of-enum status is rejected against the live CHECK, never substituted.

cases.prompt: Should cf-ralph-run-tracker invent its own write discipline for ralph_runs, or mirror an already-approved sole-writer pattern?
cases.expected_behavior: Mirror the approved cf-followup-tracker precedent — Spec v1.3 §5.5 names this skill as the sole write authority for ralph_runs 'exactly as cf-followup-tracker is for followups'. Honour the prior approved governance pattern (EQUIVALENT precedent); do not fork or invent a new pattern (SR-ANTI-03).
cases.rationale: Precedent-check case (Phase 0a / SR-DISC-06): the proposed skill has a known prior approved design (cf-followup-tracker); the build must honour it rather than drift.

cases.prompt: When the spawn is confirmed, write a Run Registry row referencing that Project with a recorded spawn timestamp in spawned_at.
cases.expected_behavior: Govern the FR-009 spawn INSERT exactly as the spec's FR-009 acceptance criterion and registry.py::record_run docstring phrase it: a ralph_runs row exists referencing the Project with spawned_at recorded.
cases.rationale: Historical-phrase case (SR-DISC-05): first build has no prior-session corpus, so the observed phrasing is sourced verbatim from the FR-009 acceptance criterion (Spec v1.3 §5.4) and the OLB-02 registry.py record_run docstring — the authoritative phrasing source for this skill's triggers.
